full_judgment: 51.	In the instant case, except a solitary statement by the respondents that the petitioner was a worker nothing was said about the working programme or the job description of an Electrical Foreman in the Corporation. In the circumstances, during the hearing of the appeal, we asked Mr. AM Aminuddin whether there is any job description or working programme of the employees of the Corporation, but he could not answer instantly. Then we allowed him time to ascertain from the Corporation whether there is any job description or working programme of its employees and after adjournment when the appeal was taken lip for hearing, Mr. Aminuddin informed us that the Corporation has neither any working programme nor any job description of an Electrical Foreman. That being the position, we have considered the definition of worker as given in clause (v) of section 2 of the Act, 1965, which appears to be almost similar with the definition of 'workman' as given in the Act, 1947. From the cited case, it further appeared that their Lordships in holding that "Foreman' is not a worker relied upon the cases of CW Raymond vs Ford Motor Co. of India Ltd (1950) 2 FJR. 1000 and Crushing (Pakistan) Limited workers Union, Lahore vs M/s Crushing (Pakistan) Limited' Workers Union, Lahore, 1962 PLC, 1275.
